R6O-bear-backcountry-0001.name: By Beatty Creek
R6O-bear-backcountry-0001.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R6O-bear-backcountry-0001.parkWhat: pull off on Hwy 51 (Telegraph Creek Rd) (gravel road)

evidence.t: Burn from 2018 (fire R91947), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SW facing slope, 13 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Beatty Creek 40 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Telegraph Creek, about 17 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Hwy 51 (Telegraph Creek Rd).
Park: 57.99978, -131.03473, pull off on Hwy 51 (Telegraph Creek Rd) (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 29 km N, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 1,815 m, about 766 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 200 m W of the spot at 858 m (58.25137, -131.17603). Water: Beatty Creek 80 m N (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-22, Region 6. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2024-10-08, closures 2026-10-16.
